sm: Georgia Howe hosts Evening Wire for Tuesday, November 24th. The Department of Health and Human Services has launched a searchable transparency website with tens of thousands of documents from agencies like the FAA, CDC and NIH, including a section on the COVID response and a previously unreleased memo about whether to leave Twitter. President Trump condemned Governor Gavin Newsom for granting clemency to 548 death row inmates, and signed an order directing the Justice Department to seek the death penalty for child murderers and for rapists and traffickers who kill victims, and to speed up federal executions. The Vatican published excerpts of Pope Francis's diary describing visions of the gates of hell and three encounters with the devil. A federal judge unsealed the search warrant against Representative Ilhan Omar, which centers on alleged immigration document falsification and a sham marriage to her brother. Iran whipped singer Parastu Ahmadi 74 times over a video of her singing without a hijab.

As many as 50 tankers carrying crude oil, liquefied petroleum and chemicals are believed to have been hit by cyber attacks, with federal officials blaming Iran. Some crews received threats that their ships would be blown up, and the Coast Guard sent cyber teams to at least four ships approaching American waters. Russia's Dmitry Medvedev wrote that outside threats could bring a preemptive nuclear strike into practical consideration, the latest of dozens of such threats since 2022. NASA's Voyager 1 became the first object to travel a full light day from Earth, but stopped sending science data, and repairs could take weeks. A possible bomb cyclone threatens the balloons at Macy's Thanksgiving parade. The Cubs signed Japanese infielder Teruaki Sato to a six-year, 120 million dollar deal.
